predecessors.name: Rasulid dynasty
predecessors.text: the Tihama lowland and the southern highlands, with Aden, that the Tahirids took over: 'They succeeded the Rasulid Dynasty' (infobox 'Established: 1454')

successors.name: Mamluk Sultanate
successors.text: 'The entire Tahirid realm' (Tihama, the southern highlands and Sana'a) 'with the exception of Aden which held out under the Tahirid governor Amir Murjan'

rulers.name: Az-Zafir Amir I bin Tahir (Salah ad-Din al-Malik az-Zafir Amir)
Al-Mansur Abd al-Wahhab bin Da'ud bin Tahir
Az-Zafir Amir II bin Abd al-Wahhab

ledger.x: 1454: Amir bin Tahir takes the title of sultan and the Tahirids succeed the Rasulids in the Tihama and the southern highlands.
1454: the brothers Amir and Ali bin Tahir take Aden.
1457: the Tahirids take Shihr on the Hadramawt coast.
ledger.cp: Shihr in Hadramawt (previous holder not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1461: Sana'a is fought over between the Tahirids and the Zaydi imams.
1466: the last dated fighting of this phase.
About 1499: Shihr is lost to the Kathiri.
1515: the second Mamluk fleet is fitted out against the Tahirids.
1517: the Mamluks end the Tahirid sultanate.

wars.name: Tahirid-Zaydi fighting for Sana'a
wars.outcome: The Tahirid army sent against the imam al-Mutawakkil al-Mutahhar was defeated in 1458; San'a was entered temporarily in 1461; the old sultan Amir was killed fighting the Zaydis in 1466; Amir II took San'a again in 1504.

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of Yemen
wars.outcome: The second Mamluk fleet under Husain al-Kurdi, equipped in 1515, took the Tahirid treasure house at al-Miqranah, beheaded Sultan Amir II near San'a on 15 May and overran the whole realm except Aden; the fleet withdrew after setting up a tributary regime in…

wars.name: Siege of Aden (1513)
wars.outcome: The Portuguese attack on Aden was beaten off by the Tahirids; no land changed hands.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier line.
